article.Citation/Title: Tomsovic, M., & Edwards, R. V. (1970). Lysergide treatment of schizophrenic and nonschizophrenic alcoholics: A controlled evaluation. Quarterly Journal of Studies on Alcohol, 31(4), 932-949.
article.InterventionDescription: Single 500 µg oral lysergide dose in a specially furnished, quiet room with music, art, and continuous nursing support; added to a 90-day inpatient VA alcoholic rehabilitation program.

ae_events.Description: Spontaneous recurrence ('recrudescence') of a lysergide-like perceptual, thought or feeling experience weeks to months after dosing; more frequent during drinking/withdrawal.
Alterations in dreaming — vivid, strongly colored dreams or fragments reliving the lysergide experience, reported as a distinct, milder phenomenon from recrudescence proper.
Two nonschizophrenic patients lost contact with reality and behaved bizarrely at the height of the lysergide session; later unable to fully recall the episode.

article.Outcome: Primary reported comparison is the nonschizophrenic lysergide-treated group vs. nonschizophrenic control group I on the two-part (abstinence/nonabstinence) Drinking Adjustment classification at 1 year, the comparison the article's own discussion foregrounds ('Table 7 shows that the nonschizophrenic lysergide-treated alcoholics were superior to all the other groups... significant beyond the .01 level'). Table 5, 12-month row: Lysergide N=32, complete abstinence (Category A) N=14 (44%); Control group I N=26, Category A N=3 (11%). Coded as '44% vs 11%'.
article.SD: Table 7, cell for Group 1 (nonschizophrenic lysergide, N=32) vs Group 2 (nonschizophrenic control I, N=26) = 7.19, footnoted as significant at the .01 level. The table's own footnote states 'Chi square for .05 level of confidence with df 1 = 3.84', confirming this is a 1-df chi-square, so coded 'χ²(1) = 7.19'.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Sum of the two compared groups' 12-month reported-case counts in Table 5 (nonschizophrenic lysergide N=32 + nonschizophrenic control group I N=26 = 58), the denominator underlying the Table 7 chi-square that produced Outcome/SD.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: No a priori or post hoc power/sample-size justification is given (sample_size_power=N), and blinding is never discussed in either direction — the open-label, unblindable coin-toss design is described, but the article never states whether raters or assessors were blinded (blinding=N). All other elements are explicitly described: objective (Methods intro), setting (VA Hospital, Sheridan, Wyo.), eligibility/recruitment (volunteers from the 90-day Program, non-acutely-psychotic per admission criteria), intervention (500 µg dose, room, procedure), comparator groups I and II, outcome measures (Drinking Adjustment Scale), randomization (coin toss pairing), statistical methods (chi-square, significance thresholds), results (Tables 3-7), harms (recrudescence study, Schwarz review citation), and funding (VA research funds, footnote 1).

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 1 because the designated primary statistic (chi²(1)=7.19, p<.01, nonschizophrenic lysergide vs. control I) was significant favoring lysergide. Flagging strong authorial caveats: the Discussion calls this comparison 'a questionable basis for assuming lysergide benefits' because control group I appears to have suffered a 'deprivation effect' (volunteers who wanted but did not receive the drug did unusually poorly), and separately states that vs. control group II (the more representative comparison, 'what was already being achieved') the abstinence difference 'was not statistically significant and we could not conclude that lysergide was beneficial.' The overall picture is genuinely mixed; 1 reflects the statistic selected as Outcome/SD per the primary-comparison precedence rule, not an unqualified positive-study verdict.
article.RandomizationYN: Coded 1 for the lysergide vs. control group I comparison: paired volunteers were assigned to lysergide or control I by coin toss ('Selection of Subjects and Controls'). Control group II was a nonrandomized historical/naturalistic comparison cohort (prior Program completers or non-volunteers), not randomized. The single binary reflects that randomization was used for part of the design.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: Coded 1: participants were drawn from the 90-day Alcoholic Rehabilitation Program and had to volunteer; the article also states an explicit exclusion basis — 'None of these patients were acutely psychotic at the time of the study or they would not have been admitted to the Alcoholic Rehabilitation Program.' No further formal medical inclusion/exclusion list (age, comorbidities) is given.
article.Retention (%): Lysergide-treated arm: 75 patients received the drug (Table 1 totals, 52 nonschizophrenic + 23 schizophrenic), treated as the randomized/allocated N since 75 already reflects post-coin-toss allocation to lysergide. At 12 months, reported cases were 32 (nonschizophrenic, Table 5) + 12 (schizophrenic, Table 6) = 44. 44/75 × 100 = 58.7%.
article.BaseStatus: Coded 'Severe': inpatient VA 90-day Alcoholic Rehabilitation Program admission, mean years of problem drinking ~10-13 years across groups (Table 2), and substantial psychiatric comorbidity (23/75 lysergide-treated diagnosed schizophrenic; Table 1 subtypes include antisocial personality, chronic brain syndrome, drug addiction).
article.Age_Median: Table 2 reports mean ages of 43-45 across the nonschizophrenic lysergide and control subgroups at both the 3-month and 1-year timepoints; falls in the '30-50' bracket. Age was not separately tabulated for the schizophrenic subgroups ('number was too small for meaningful analysis').
article.PercentFem: Not reported anywhere in the article. This is a Veterans Administration hospital inpatient program (1965-1968 era), which strongly implies a near-entirely male sample, but since no explicit figure or statement is given, coded '.' rather than inferred.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Not reported anywhere in the article.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Veterans Administration Hospital, Sheridan, Wyoming, USA.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: sample was self-selected volunteers from a single VA inpatient program, and the authors themselves note this volunteer self-selection likely biased control group I ('a self-selected group of patients who have a poor prognosis because of their strong propensity to value a drug cure').
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: Coded 1 for the Blewett and Chwelos Scales for the Assessment of Psychedelic Reactions (Scales 1 and 2), a named psychometric instrument used to assess the drug experience and post-treatment attitude change. The Drinking Adjustment Scale used for the primary outcome was study-specific, not a named validated instrument.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Coded 0: the Blewett and Chwelos scales assess psychedelic-experience phenomenology and personality/attitude change ('intellectual', 'emotional', 'spiritual' insight), not clinical depression/anxiety/PTSD/well-being constructs, so distinguished from a mental-health outcome measure.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 1: drinking control was tracked longitudinally at 3, 6 and 12 months per patient, explicitly showing 'a typical erosion of drinking control in the course of a year' — i.e., return-to-use over time was tracked, not just a single endpoint status.
article.MortalityMeasured: Coded 0. The only mention of death is in the attrition discussion — 'A few patients died and about one-third had to be removed for methodological reasons' — given as a reason for loss of contact across all six study groups (including the two non-lysergide control groups), with no count, no attribution to lysergide, and no linkage to the article's dedicated harms discussion (which addresses only recrudescence and states 'None of our lysergide-treated patients... suffered any of these serious aftereffects'). Judged not to constitute a reported mortality outcome or AE of the intervention; flagged here as a non-obvious call rather than silently coding 1 with a fabricated AE entry.
article.ArmScope: All reported AE information (recrudescence, altered dreaming, in-session dissociative episodes) is drawn exclusively from the 75 lysergide-treated patients; no AE data are reported for control groups I or II.
article.AE_denominator: No single safety-population denominator is stated. Recrudescence was assessed over '61 patients who gave information on the absence or presence of recrudescence' (out of 75 lysergide-treated); the 2-patient in-session dissociation report and the 7-patient altered-dreaming report do not state their own denominators. Coded 'Not numbered' because denominators differ by AE type and no unified figure is given.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Not calculable as a single unduplicated count: the recrudescence (19), altered-dreaming (7) and in-session dissociation (2) groups may overlap, and the article gives no combined tally of unique patients with ≥1 AE.

ae_events.Tomsovic 1970_AE01: NAffected=19 and onset timing from 'Of the 19 patients who reported single or multiple recrudescences, 3 had the first within a few weeks... 12 (65%) reported the first on the 3-month follow-up questionnaire, 3 (15%) on the 6-month, and 1 on the 12-month' — first occurrence generally weeks to months out, coded 'delayed'. Severity graded Mild per rubric (pre-1980 article, no CTCAE existed): described as 'relatively brief experiences that varied from very uncomfortable to very pleasant,' with no intervention or lasting impairment reported, so SeveritySource='rubric', not 'author' (authors used no formal severity/SAE language for this event).
ae_events.Tomsovic 1970_AE02: Reported as 'An additional group of 7 patients (11%) reported that they experienced alterations in dreaming,' distinct from the 19-patient recrudescence group, and explicitly called 'questionable examples of recrudescence' by the authors rather than merged into that count — kept as its own AE type. No onset timing is given for this subgroup specifically (unlike the 3/6/12-month breakdown given for recrudescence), so Onset is coded 'unknown' rather than inferred. Graded Mild per rubric: transient, non-intervention-requiring sleep-related phenomenon.
ae_events.Tomsovic 1970_AE03: SeverityIndeterminate='Y' because the article gives no information on whether any pharmacological or clinical intervention was used for the two patients who 'lost contact with reality... and acted bizarrely' and 'could not completely recall what had happened,' nor how long the disorientation/amnesia persisted beyond the session. Graded Moderate rather than the rubric's under-specified-AE default of Mild because the authors themselves flagged it as a concerning departure from the expected reaction ('gave us concern'), which exceeds ordinary transient anxiety/perceptual distortion, but nothing in the text meets an FDA seriousness criterion (no hospitalization, life-threat, or persistent disability documented), so MeetsFDASerious='N'. AE_type coded 'both': the event occurred in-session as acute drug-effect phenomenology but was also treated by the investigators as a clinically notable adverse occurrence.

config_proposal.note: χ²(1)=7.19 (Table 7) comparing nonschizophrenic lysergide-treated (n=32) vs. nonschizophrenic control group I (n=26) on 1-year abstinence/nonabstinence classification. The article explicitly states the applicable critical value is for df=1 ('Chi square for .05 level of confidence with df 1 = 3.84'), confirming a genuine 1-df 2x2 comparison, so convert_to_d()'s 1-df assumption holds cleanly here. Direction=1 because the result favors lysergide (higher abstinence). Note the authors themselves question the validity of this specific comparison (possible 'deprivation effect' inflating the gap via control group I's unusually poor outcomes), which is a substantive caveat for methodologist review even though the statistic itself converts cleanly.
